rubric_notes: Meets all must_include items: SCOPe 2.08 a.22.1 with families a.22.1.1-4 and a.22.1.0 (sunids verified in bundle), superfamily = probable common ancestry, family distinctions kept and function transfer rejected. Correctly notes a.22 has a single superfamily. Linker histone a.4.5.13 and HU/IHF a.55.1.1 placements verified. Deduction: asserts HU/IHF similarity is 'convergent function, not shared ancestry' and H1/H5 'are not homologous' as fact, which SCOPe placement alone does not establish (should be 'no homology claim'). Periodic-update label not in this bundle but consistent with the release record. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families a.204.1.2 / a.204.1.4 and superfamily a.204.1 (resolve endpoints in bundle). Family/fold/class sunids and protein names are not in the bundle (search returned empty) but are accurate. Remote homology interpreted correctly; explicitly rejects HisE and MazG function transfer, notes boundary difference and representative caveats. Minor: attributes an acidic Mg2+ motif basis to SCOPe's judgement from general knowledge. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Families, superfamily, fold description, class and c.55 superfamily list all supported by evidence; 15 named families plus automated matches is correct. Explains superfamily-level homology as probable common ancestry beyond shape, with shared core, phosphate loops and hinge closure; explicitly refuses transfer of specific function, substrate, regulation, oligomeric/polymer state, cellular role, EC numbers, partners. Fold-level similarity correctly limited. Lists external evidence needed. Minor paraphrase of the duplication comment is immaterial. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Families, sunids, members, L. plantarum species and other a.25 superfamilies supported. Stable-label and periodic-update claims not backed by any /releases/current response in bundle. Reasoning complete: superfamily = probable common ancestry via conserved metal site, family-level chemical divergence, fold weaker, no cross-family transfer, experimental evidence required, domain-vs-whole-protein caveat. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Three families with correct sccs and sunids; example domains d1ikop_ and d5n0ya1 (A:3-112), PAD4 middle (b.2.9.1) and catalytic (d.126.1.5) domains, and b.6.2 SAG1 all supported by search/resolve bundle entries. Correctly interprets superfamily as probable distant ancestry contrasted with fold-only SAG1, rejects copper/electron-transfer inference for ephrin and PAD4, lists ligand-set alignment and direct experimental metal/redox evidence required, and limits templates to fold level. Honest that curator comments were not retrieved and that examples are illustrative. Complete.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Classifications, Pfam cross-references and the fold core comment are all supported by the bundle. Biological reasoning is complete: superfamily = probable common ancestor, fold-level neighbours lack demonstrated ancestry, family-level divergence explained, all named unsafe transfers rejected including within-family conjugation and GTPase-specificity caveats, external evidence listed. Factual support marked down one step for the confusing self-correction 'sunid 63263 is wrong; the correct sunid is 54263', a stray incorrect identifier left in the text even though the final value is right.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Families, sunids, domain boundaries (d1orda1 1-107, d1r8ja2 2-135, d1r8ja1 a.186.1.1 177-282) and c.67.1 PLP-dependent transferases resolve correctly. Reasoning complete: superfamily-level remote ancestry, fold insufficient, explicit domain-cut/multidomain caveat, rejection of phosphorylation, catalysis and partner transfer in both directions, template limits, external evidence listed. Noncentral factual error: states the c.67.1.5 catalytic domain is in 'a different class and fold'; c.67 is a different fold but the same class c (a/b). 1ord d1orda2/d1orda3 details are correct but not in the cited bundle.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Hierarchy, species for both proteins, example domains and boundaries, PubMed citation, empty Pfam/UniProt xrefs all supported. Reasoning complete: fold-level similarity not a homology claim, no claim either way about b.84.1-b.84.4, family-level homology of V1/A1 is the strong claim, rest of A subunit classified elsewhere. Imprecision: describes bulge as inserted 'within the N-terminal beta-barrel region' whereas SCOPe shows it splitting the c.37.1.11 P-loop domain. Periodic update label not in this bundle but consistent with the current release metadata; noted only.

Superfamilies and sunids supported by resolve calls. Correct fold-vs-superfamily conclusion, good unsafe-transfer list, and evidence requirements (HMM-HMM, equivalent ligand positions, quinone sites). Leans toward 'fold-level analogy' and 'convergent solution' framing without stating that remote homology remains possible or that separate superfamilies do not prove unrelatedness, so calibration is incomplete. Release label, periodic-update date, and the f.21.4 404 check are asserted without supporting bundle entries. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Complete and evidence-backed: sunids, fold comments, family comment, PF02254, sibling family numbers all match the bundle. Interprets superfamily as remote homology, family as the level of sequence/functional coherence, fold as architecture only; correctly handles the 'next two folds' comment. Explains ADH family defined by GroES-like partner domain, CoA domain binds CoA in ligase, RCK domains are allosteric sensors. Bars cross-family function/ligand transfer, addresses templates, representatives, automated matches and external evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct lineage and sunids from resolve/parents endpoints; correct calibrated conclusion (shared labels in class k reflect design similarity, not homology) with good transfer limits and discussion of low-complexity heptad repeats. Missing the explicit 'not a true family' annotation on family 100905; no annotation endpoint was consulted.

All must_include met: 1.69 d1t1ja_ in own fold c.137.1.1 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1/d1f8ya_ share c.23.14 but remain c.23.14.2/c.23.14.1; change framed as recognition of distant homology (probable common ancestry, stronger than fold), with sunids preserved and superfamily renamed. Correctly separates the SID suffix change (l.1.1.1 tag split d1t1ja2 A:0, d1t1jb2 B:-6-0) from the biological reclassification. Pinpoints 1.71 as first release with new placement (bundle-supported). Limits on function/template transfer stated. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct l.1.1.1 artifact classification with sunids, correct d1a14h1 H:9-111 b.1.1.1, tag similarity rejected, and good level-based homology explanation. However it argues from DBREF (not visible in the truncated bundle) that residues 1-8 are native and that 'biologically, the whole VH domain is residues 1-111', in tension with the gold view that H:9-111 is the biological domain and with must_avoid on placing the tag in the biological family; appropriately says not to treat the match as homology evidence either way. Release claim '2.08-stable; freeze date 2021-07-28' is unsupported by any bundle response. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1; 2026-10-14.

Release-specific support is complete and correct: 1.75 whole-chain d1acca_ with full lineage sunids, unchanged in 2.01-2.03, split from 2.04 through 2.08 into d1acca2 (A:14-225, b.179.1.1) and d1acca1 (A:226-735, f.60.1.1), f.11 retired. Module interpretation and per-level semantics are otherwise well handled, and toxin functions are not transferred from a PA14 hit. Decisive flaw: it flatly states there is no homology between the N- and C-terminal parts, inferring absence of common ancestry from separate superfamily placement alone. The suggested relationship of the f.60 region to clostridial binary-toxin B components is also asserted beyond the retrieved classification.

Complete: correct five-domain decomposition with boundaries and sccs, new fold d.394 for d3jb9a5, sister-family context for e.8.1, c.52.1, c.55.3 and a.29.2.1 all supported by bundle, S. cerevisiae 4i43 family-mates supported, d.394 present in 2.07 supported. Clear reuse-vs-innovation interpretation, weighs evidence by hierarchy level, rejects catalytic and acetyl-lysine transfer, notes Jab1/MPN not covered. 2.06 404 claim is unverifiable from bundle (successful responses only) but plausible and noncentral. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14.

Good core reasoning: shared family, repeat-unit homology with conserved motifs, length set by construct repeat count, plus sound limits on target-site transfer, BurrH's different biological context, template choice and representative selection. Two decisive problems. It omits the 're' heterogeneity annotation and the canonical repeat unit 4cj9 A:259-292 entirely, leaving the annotation-interpretation criterion unmet. It also asserts the family 'contains three separate protein entries, one for each domain', which misstates the family's content (additional protein nodes exist, including PthXo1 and automated matches) and is unsupported by its evidence. Evaluator: Claude SCOPe benchmark grader, 2026-10-14.

Correct, supported metadata and periodic label. Cites stable 2.08 / 2.08-stable, preserves dated label if periodic layer used, rejects 'current'/'latest'. Periodic semantics correct: incremental update adding newer automatically classified PDB entries, no new freeze, no manual re-curation of the hierarchy. Statements about 2.07 labels and absence of stable/periodic labels for 2.01 and SCOP 1.x are supported by the releases bundle. Extra homology caveats are not required but not wrong. Complete.

All must_include items met: shared a.47.2.1 lineage for fragments and d1dn1b_; fragment comment and 'ms' flag cited from 2.08 annotations with 1.75 comparison; a.47 defined as four long helices so three-helix fragments cannot show the fold on their own and their fold label is inherited from full-domain homologs; d1dn1b_ history (curated 17771 in 1.75, absent 2.01, automated match to d3c98b_ from 2.06) and curated d3c98b_ reference all supported by bundle. Correctly separates fold-level similarity (a.47.1 STAT) from superfamily homology, lists unsafe transfers and external evidence. Minor stylistic overreach calling three-helix resemblance 'convergence', but not asserted from superfamily placement. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Convergence stated as 'most parsimonious' with explicit caveat that separate superfamilies mean 'no convincing evidence of common ancestry', not proven unrelatedness; divergence confined to superfamily/family. Level semantics correct. Evidence integration complete (HMM E-values, whole-core structural similarity vs fold background, idiosyncratic features, domain architecture, phylogeny). Broad lineage coverage (c.2, c.3, c.4, c.31.1.5, d.58.20.1, e.52.1, DNA ligase domains, b.35.1, d.81.1) supported by the search bundle or correct general knowledge; release and periodic-update labels correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Release comparison and hierarchy are right: 2.04 lineages with both superfamilies named, 2.08 new family b.18.1.36 under b.18.1 with Cry3A unchanged in b.18.1.3, sunids retained, chain B split with the l.1.1.1 segment, and the per-release check showing b.18.1.36 from 2.05 onward. Interpretation is accurate and well bounded: superfamily means probable ancestry not shared function, 'galactose-binding' is a label not a measured activity, neither domain is a sound template for the other, and same-family templates and correct representative domains are specified. Factual deduction because the detailed structure-comparison figures, including the weaker Cry domain-III match and the CUB-like comparison, are presented as retrieved although the representative's hit response is not in this answer's bundle, which holds only the empty 1nqdA list and release domain listings. The curated family comment citing the relevant publication was not retrieved, and the answer notes the rationale literature was not consulted. Evaluator: Claude, 2026-10-14.

Uses retrieved SEQRES sequences to show the exact differences (L16A, K52E, C-terminal KIKK vs KIRRS over 53 shared residues), which is correct. Lineage, sunids, boundaries, comments, hf definition and tag-domain split are correct. Clear argument that classification follows sequence while geometry does not; rejects template use in both directions; addresses training labels, leakage, representatives and function; attributes folding-intermediate interpretation to literature, not the API.

Reasoning complete: valid but incomplete family member; 99 SEQRES vs 50 ATOM residues with missing stretches identified; coverage-aware structural/sequence alignment and masking; complete domain-2 entry for tissue factor and d1uc6a1 for CNTFR as representatives; fragment excluded or included only with masking and coverage weighting; family vs superfamily vs fold strength distinguished; no function transfer. Factual gaps: never cites the fr annotation record; family/superfamily/protein sunids, 1o5d chain H/L classifications, d1o5dt1 range and 2.08-stable label asserted without supporting endpoints in its bundle (values are correct, not fabricated); no quality values retrieved for either entry. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Reasoning complete: correct level semantics, new superfamily in existing fold, family = homology claim, new fold = different core topology, revisable hypothesis with specific evidence types, no cross-fold function transfer. Slight shorthand that same-fold/different-superfamily pairs 'are not true remote homologs' overstates SCOPe's non-assertion, but core reasoning correctly allows undetectable homology. Factual: d.58 sunid and listed superfamilies d.58.1/6/7/17/18 supported; later superfamilies (d.58.58, d.58.63-65) and count of 62 fall beyond the truncated bundle but are plausibly from the full children response (has_more false). The periodic update label 2.08-2026-08-16 is not supported by any cited endpoint in the bundle.

All three families and sunids correct and supported; cites the superfamily homology record (sf scope), fold and family annotations, and the ATP-grasp/PIPK comment correctly as similarity rather than homology. Distinguishes family-level versus superfamily-level homology, infers shared bilobal core and catalytic motifs, and rejects transfer of substrate type and regulation across families. Requires family/subfamily assignment, catalytic-motif conservation, specificity/regulatory residue conservation via structure-based alignment, domain architecture, and direct biochemistry.
